newsitem.title: USA: Darden expects Q2 to be unprofitable.
newsitem.headline: Darden expects Q2 to be unprofitable.

text.p: Darden Restaurants Inc said Thursday it expects its second fiscal quarter to be unprofitable.
Earlier this week Darden said it was cutting menu prices at its Red Lobster restaurants and committing $150 million to redecorate these restaurants.

"Because of one-time costs to implement the changes at Red Lobster and the time required for customer traffic to build... we expect Darden's second fiscal quarter to be unprofitable," Chief Executive Officer Joe Lee said.

Darden reported first quarter earnings after tax were $20.5 million or $0.13 a share, compared to earnings after tax, but before restructuring charges, of $32.8 million or $0.21 per share in the first quarter of fiscal 1996.
It attributed the decline to "significantly lower earnings at Red Lobster."
In last year's first quarter, the company recorded a $75 million pre-tax restructuring charge, $44.8 million after tax or $0.28 per share, to discontinue its China Coast stores.
After this unusual item, last year's first quarter showed a net loss of $12.1 million or $0.08 per share.
Darden's sales for the first quarter declined 3.6 percent from the year ago to $805.6 million.
It said about half the sales decline related to the discontinued China Coast stores which were closed last August, and the rest was attributable to Red Lobster.
"The first quarter operating results are very disappointing, but I believe we have the right strategies and action plans in place to improve Red Lobster's performance," Lee said.
